answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent validators confirm fraud or duplicate claims. Creating a hundred sybils therefore means funding a hundred bonds, not merely minting names; captured stake can reward honest reporters. The sonnet of one identity may ripple through a voyage of tasks, but copying it across accounts risks losing every bond, so the attack becomes capital-intensive and costly to sustain.
